extracted.intended_audience: Medicare advocacy organizations and health policy advocates who submit comments to CMS and other federal agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting effective notice-and-comment letters and sign-on letters addressing Medicare rules, including structure, evidence, coordination, and common pitfalls. Focused on advocacy organizations submitting comments to CMS or similar agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the organization, its mission, and constituency
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the organization, its mission, and constituency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish standing and credibility up front; describe who you represent (e.g., beneficiaries, providers) and why your perspective matters to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the docket number and rule being addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: State the docket number and rule being addressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the agency can readily associate the submission with the correct rulemaking record by providing docket identifiers and clear references to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an overview of position (support/oppose/conditional)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize your overall stance at the start so reviewers immediately understand your perspective; expand substantively later in the letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify the specific proposed change being addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific proposed change being addressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing issues, clearly link comments to particular proposed provisions or regulatory text instead of speaking only in generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the current state and why change is being considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The current state and why change is being considered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context on existing policy/practice and the agency's stated reasons for proposing change to show you engaged with the rule's background and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the organization's position with reasoning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain not just what you want but why — include legal, clinical, programmatic, or beneficiary-impact rationales that support your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include beneficiary/patient impact stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use individual stories to illustrate real-world effects; combine narrative evidence with aggregate data to strengthen claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite research/data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with empirical evidence; provide full citations (not just abstracts) and, where possible, link to sources or append supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide suggested alternative regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer specific replacement language or edits to the proposed rule to make it easier for the agency to adopt your recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of key positions in closing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End with a concise recap of your major recommendations so reviewers leaving the record can quickly grasp your asks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer to provide additional information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express willingness to supply further data, examples, or technical assistance; this can facilitate follow-up engagement with the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contact information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear contact details for follow-up and to establish an official point of contact for the submitting organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show breadth of constituency in sign-on letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Show breadth of constituency (consumers + providers + payers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate wide support by including diverse stakeholder types to increase credibility and political impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include national, state, and local organizations in sign-ons
rubrics_metrics.description: Include national, state, and local organizations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mix of organizational scales signals broad geographic and practice-area reach; name organizations and their jurisdictions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite each organization's distinct expertise in sign-ons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why each signatory adds value (e.g., clinical expertise, consumer representation, actuarial analysis) rather than just listing names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistent messaging while preserving organizational voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistent messaging while preserving organizational voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate wording so key asks align across signatories, but allow each organization to retain brief individualized language reflecting its mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate release of sign-on letters with media outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are released coordinated with media outreach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing sign-on releases with media can amplify impact; plan public messaging and embargoes as part of coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific Medicare statutes and Code of Federal Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific Medicare statutes and Code of Federal Regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground legal arguments in statute and regulation citations so agency reviewers can evaluate compliance and legal constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with CMS's stated rationale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly respond to the agency's reasoning and evidence in the rulemaking record rather than making unrelated assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide both individual stories AND aggregate data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both individual stories AND aggregate data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine qualitative anecdotes with quantitative evidence to demonstrate both human impact and scope/magnitude of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address health equity dimensions explicitly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss disparate impacts across populations and include equity-related evidence, metrics, or recommendations to mitigate harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed clinical literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-quality clinical studies where relevant to support clinical or coverage-related recommendations; provide full bibliographic details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address coverage, payment, AND program integrity dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Address coverage, payment, AND program integrity dimensions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the full policy ecosystem: how changes affect beneficiary access, reimbursement incentives, and program safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge complexities and trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limitations, competing objectives, and potential unintended consequences to demonstrate balanced, realistic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest specific implementation timelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feasible timelines for phased implementation or delays where appropriate to reduce disruption and aid agency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure expressions of support/opposition without analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure expressions of support/opposition without analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't submit form letters that merely state a position; substantiate statements with facts, law, and concrete recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ignore the agency's specific questions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the targeted questions posed in the notice; structured responses keyed to each question are more useful to agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full citations, not only abstracts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid weak sourcing; include full references and, when possible, source documents or data appendices to allow verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the cost/benefit framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to address the cost/benefit framework
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with economic analyses or offer data/estimates about costs and benefits if relevant to the rule's regulatory impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic language usable for any rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic language usable for any rule
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor comments to the specific rule, provisions, and populations affected; avoid boilerplate that offers little value to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the comment deadline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within the official comment period; late submissions are less likely to be considered and may be excluded from the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redact PHI; do not include unredacted protected health information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect patient privacy by removing or anonymizing any protected health information before public submission.
